**Finding: deviation (Section 7.2, p0026)**

Section 7.2 requires us to disclose and match any more favourable competing offer before engaging another provider — a right of first refusal that functions as exclusivity binding the Customer. It fails the fallback on every material term: no defined product/service category, no 12-month limit, and no automatic termination on Vendor's service-level or delivery failures, so it runs for the full three-year term with no performance-based exit (walk-away territory). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment.

Validated redline (preferred position) replaces the gate with an express confirmation of our sourcing freedom. The MFN/pricing-disclosure angle is left to the MFN rule, and the Customer non-compete (second 12.4) and minimum-volume commitment (2.1) are for their own rules.
